description: Build a shell-native visual IDE that turns a Solidity codebase into a live, interactive graph of files, contracts, functions, relationships, edits, and Foundry test activity. The graph is the primary interface while source code remains available for inspection.

userStories.title: Create the application workspace
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want a TypeScript workspace for the CLI, local service, shared graph model, and web UI so later features have a maintainable foundation.
acceptanceCriteria: The repository contains separate packages or applications for the CLI/local service, web UI, and shared graph types
A single documented install command installs all workspace dependencies
Root scripts run type checking, tests, and production builds across the workspace
A minimal web page can be started locally from a root script
README documents prerequisites and local development commands
All automated tests, type checks, and builds pass
userStories.notes: Use React and TypeScript for the web UI and Node.js with TypeScript for the CLI/local service. Keep the initial workspace minimal.

userStories.title: Define the unified graph model
userStories.description: As a feature developer, I want a language-independent graph schema so static analysis, runtime events, and future language adapters can use the same representation.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared types define graph nodes, graph edges, source locations, node statuses, and serializable metadata
Node kinds include repository, directory, file, contract, function, modifier, event, test, task, command, and finding
Edge kinds include contains, imports, inherits, calls, reads, writes, applies_modifier, tests, and modifies
Statuses include idle, planned, inspecting, active, passed, failed, warning, and deleted
Runtime validation rejects malformed graph payloads with actionable errors
Unit tests cover valid graphs, invalid references, duplicate IDs, and serialization
userStories.notes: Stable IDs must be deterministic for the same repository content so UI state survives re-analysis.

userStories.title: Add a Solidity analysis fixture
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want a small representative Solidity project fixture so analyzers and visual behavior can be tested deterministically.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture project contains at least two imported Solidity files and two related contracts
The fixture demonstrates inheritance, public and internal functions, a modifier, state reads and writes, an event, a custom error, and an external call
The fixture includes Foundry tests with both passing and intentionally failing test cases
Fixture source is documented as test data and is not included in production builds
An automated check confirms the expected fixture files are available
userStories.notes: Keep the contracts deliberately small; they exist to cover analysis behavior, not to model production-safe financial logic.

userStories.title: Discover Solidity source files
userStories.description: As a Solidity developer, I want the tool to discover source files from a project path so I can analyze a repository without manual configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: The analyzer accepts an absolute or relative project directory
It recursively discovers .sol files while ignoring .git, node_modules, out, cache, and configurable ignored paths
All returned paths are normalized relative to the project root and sorted deterministically
Missing directories, unreadable paths, and projects with no Solidity files produce actionable errors
Unit tests cover discovery, default ignores, custom ignores, and error cases
userStories.notes: Do not require the target project to be a Foundry project for static discovery.

userStories.title: Parse Solidity files into structural nodes
userStories.description: As a Solidity developer, I want files, contracts, functions, modifiers, events, errors, and state variables extracted so I can inspect code structure visually.
acceptanceCriteria: Analysis uses Solidity compiler output or a compatible Solidity AST rather than regular expressions
The fixture produces nodes for source files, contracts, functions, modifiers, events, custom errors, and state variables
Contract metadata includes kind and inheritance names; function metadata includes visibility, mutability, and payable state
Every source-backed node contains an accurate file, start position, and end position
Parser diagnostics include file and source location when available
Snapshot or equivalent tests verify deterministic output for the fixture
userStories.notes: Preserve compiler diagnostics rather than silently dropping files that fail to parse.

userStories.title: Build Solidity dependency relationships
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want imports, containment, and inheritance represented as graph edges so I can understand the codebase architecture.
acceptanceCriteria: The graph contains repository, directory, file, and contract hierarchy using contains edges
Resolved Solidity imports create imports edges between file nodes
Resolved base contracts create inherits edges between contract nodes
Unresolved imports or inheritance references are reported as diagnostics without crashing analysis
Duplicate relationships are not emitted
Automated tests verify all expected fixture relationships
userStories.notes: Keep unresolved references visible in diagnostics so users can distinguish incomplete analysis from missing relationships.

userStories.title: Analyze function behavior
userStories.description: As a smart-contract reviewer, I want calls, state access, modifiers, and value-related behavior mapped so I can see security-relevant interactions.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolved internal and external function invocations create calls edges
State-variable access creates distinct reads and writes edges
Modifier usage creates applies_modifier edges
Function metadata identifies external calls and value-sending calls when the AST provides enough evidence
Ambiguous or unresolved calls are retained as diagnostics or explicitly marked metadata rather than guessed
Automated tests verify the fixture's calls, reads, writes, modifier usage, and value-related metadata
userStories.notes: Static analysis is evidence, not proof of runtime behavior. The UI must later label it accordingly.

userStories.title: Expose analysis through the shell
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run one command in a Solidity repository and receive a graph so the product is useful from the shell.
acceptanceCriteria: A codevis analyze [path] command analyzes the supplied path or the current directory by default
The command can write the validated graph as JSON to stdout or a requested output file
Human-readable progress and diagnostics go to stderr so stdout remains machine-readable
The command exits non-zero for invalid input or analysis failure and zero for successful analysis
codevis --help documents command usage and available options
An integration test analyzes the fixture and validates the resulting graph
userStories.notes: The executable may initially run through the workspace package script, but its public command name must be codevis.

userStories.title: Render the repository graph
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an interactive visual map of the analyzed repository so the system is understandable without reading every file.
acceptanceCriteria: The web UI loads a graph from the local service and renders nodes and directed edges on an interactive canvas
Files, contracts, functions, modifiers, events, tests, and findings have visually distinct node treatments
Import, inheritance, call, read, write, test, and containment relationships can be visually distinguished
Users can pan, zoom, fit the graph to view, and reset the viewport
Loading, empty, and analysis-error states are clearly displayed
The fixture graph is verified with component tests and a browser smoke test
userStories.notes: Use React Flow or an equivalent maintained graph canvas. Prioritize clarity over decorative animation.

userStories.title: Add progressive graph detail
userStories.description: As a developer working in a large repository, I want to expand and collapse code structure so I can move between architecture and function-level detail.
acceptanceCriteria: The initial repository view groups or collapses function-level nodes under their owning file or contract
Users can expand a file or contract to reveal its contained nodes and collapse it again
Edges connected to hidden nodes are summarized or hidden without pointing to nonexistent visible endpoints
Expansion state remains stable while the same graph is open
A fit-to-selection action focuses the viewport on an expanded group
Component tests cover expand, collapse, and connected-edge behavior
userStories.notes: This is the first defense against unusable hairball graphs; avoid rendering every node by default.

userStories.title: Inspect nodes and source code
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want to select a visual node and inspect its concrete source evidence so every diagram element remains trustworthy.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a node opens a detail panel with its kind, status, metadata, and incoming and outgoing relationships
Source-backed nodes show the relevant source excerpt with the node's source range highlighted
The panel displays the repository-relative file path and line numbers
A copy-location action copies a path:line reference
Nodes without source locations show an explicit explanation instead of a broken source view
Component tests cover source-backed and source-less node inspection
userStories.notes: Reading source is secondary to the graph but must always be one selection away.

userStories.title: Filter and search the graph
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want to find symbols and isolate relationship types so I can answer focused questions in a nontrivial codebase.
acceptanceCriteria: Search matches node labels and repository-relative paths without case sensitivity
Selecting a search result reveals hidden ancestors, selects the node, and focuses the viewport
Users can toggle node kinds and edge kinds independently
A security-focused preset shows external calls, state writes, value-related functions, and findings
A clear-filters action restores the default view
Component tests verify search, focus, filter toggles, preset behavior, and reset
userStories.notes: The security preset is a view over evidence, not an automated vulnerability verdict.

userStories.title: Launch the visualizer with a watch command
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one shell command to start the local service and UI for my repository so the visual IDE is easy to enter.
acceptanceCriteria: A codevis watch [path] command starts the local analysis service and serves the web UI
The command prints the local URL and analyzed project path
The service binds to loopback by default and supports a configurable available port
The UI receives the initial validated graph without requiring a manual file import
SIGINT and SIGTERM close the HTTP server and filesystem resources cleanly
An integration test starts the command against the fixture, fetches the UI and graph, and shuts it down
userStories.notes: Do not expose repository source over a non-loopback interface by default.

userStories.title: Visualize live file changes
userStories.description: As a developer coding manually or with an agent, I want the graph to react to file changes so I can see which part of the system is being changed.
acceptanceCriteria: The watch service detects created, modified, and deleted Solidity files using the same ignore rules as static discovery
Changes trigger a debounced incremental or full re-analysis without restarting the service
Graph updates are pushed to connected browsers over a live transport
Affected nodes visibly transition through active to completed, warning, failed, or deleted states
Rapid writes do not produce overlapping analyses or stale graph updates
Integration tests cover create, modify, delete, syntax-error, and recovery flows
userStories.notes: WebSockets or server-sent events are acceptable. Favor correctness and ordered updates over premature incremental-analysis optimization.

userStories.title: Record and display work events
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a timeline of analysis and work states so I can understand what the tool or coding agent is doing over time.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned event schema supports plan created, step started, file read, file edit started, file edit completed, command started, test passed, test failed, finding created, and work completed
The local service records filesystem and analysis activity as timestamped events for the current session
The UI shows a chronological timeline with event type, message, timestamp, and linked graph targets
Selecting a linked event reveals and focuses its target nodes
Malformed external events are rejected without interrupting the active session
Unit and component tests cover schema validation, ordering, rendering, and graph linking
userStories.notes: Define the protocol independently of terminal-text parsing so agents can emit semantic events later. Persistent session history is out of scope for this story.

userStories.title: Discover and run Foundry tests
userStories.description: As a Solidity developer, I want to run Foundry tests from the visualizer so test activity is connected to the contracts it validates.
acceptanceCriteria: The tool detects whether forge is available and whether the selected repository is a Foundry project
A codevis test [optional test filter] command runs tests without invoking a shell interpreter with unsanitized user input
Foundry JSON or another stable machine-readable output is parsed into test names, duration, pass, fail, and skipped results
Compiler errors, test failures, and missing Foundry prerequisites produce actionable diagnostics
The command exits non-zero when compilation or tests fail
Integration tests use the fixture or recorded deterministic Foundry output and cover passing, failing, filtered, and unavailable cases
userStories.notes: Keep command execution local and explicit. Wallets and public-chain transactions are not part of the MVP.

userStories.title: Map Foundry results onto the graph
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want tests and failures connected to affected code so I can see verification coverage and failures in context.
acceptanceCriteria: Discovered tests appear as test nodes with tests edges to resolved contracts or functions
Running tests from the UI or CLI streams started, passed, failed, and completed events to the live session
Active tests animate their nodes and relevant edges; completed tests become green and failed tests become red
Failure messages and compiler diagnostics are attached to the most specific resolvable graph node and shown in its detail panel
Unresolved test targets and diagnostics remain accessible in the timeline
Integration and browser tests verify passing, failing, and unresolved result visualization
userStories.notes: Runtime-observed relationships must look different from statically inferred relationships.

userStories.title: Deliver the Solidity-first MVP workflow
userStories.description: As a new user, I want a polished end-to-end workflow and sample project so I can understand and evaluate the visualizer quickly.
acceptanceCriteria: README provides installation, codevis analyze, codevis watch, and codevis test walkthroughs
A documented demo flow opens the fixture, explores a contract and function, edits a file, and observes a Foundry test result
The UI explains the visual legend for node kinds, edge kinds, static relationships, runtime relationships, and statuses
No-data, missing-tool, compiler-error, and disconnected-live-session states offer a recovery action
An end-to-end smoke test covers launching from the shell through rendering the fixture graph and receiving one live update
All workspace tests, type checks, lint checks, production builds, and the end-to-end smoke test pass
userStories.notes: MVP completion excludes wallet connection, public-chain interaction, Slither integration, persistent sessions, non-Solidity languages, and drag-and-drop code generation.
